methodology: Use SentenceTransformer.encode as the inference entry point, represent sentence1 and sentence2 independently as normalized MiniLM sentence embeddings, and score paraphrase decisions by cosine-similarity thresholding, differing from all cross-encoder and prompted methods by using a bi-encoder retrieval-style pipeline with no cross-token interaction at inference time.
plan: 1) In one code cell install sentence-transformers, datasets, scikit-learn, and tqdm; 2) import torch, numpy, load_dataset, SentenceTransformer, accuracy_score, f1_score, classification_report, and tqdm; 3) set device to 'mps' when available else 'cpu' and print it; 4) choose model_name = 'sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2' and load SentenceTransformer(model_name, device=device); 5) load glue/mrpc validation and extract sentence1, sentence2, and y_true; 6) encode sentence1 and sentence2 separately in batches with convert_to_tensor=True, normalize_embeddings=True, and a batch size around 128; 7) compute cosine similarities by elementwise multiplying normalized embeddings and summing across dimensions; 8) apply one fixed threshold chosen a priori, such as 0.80, to obtain binary y_pred without any tuning loop; 9) move scores to CPU numpy arrays and compute accuracy, F1, and classification_report; 10) print a few examples with similarity scores plus the first 10 mistakes; 11) build a summary dict with dataset, split, model, device, threshold, num_examples, accuracy, and f1.
